title: Useful Lifetime, Replacement and Interruption Figures for Durable Medical Equipment Rentals
content:
Two sets of figures govern how long a Durable Medical Equipment Rentals item is expected to serve and when a pause in medical need resets the rental: the reasonable useful lifetime with its replacement terms, and the interruption length after which a new rental period and cap start.

## Figures by payment class

| Payment class | Reasonable useful lifetime (months before like-for-like replacement is payable) | Replacement payable after the lifetime | Replacement payable earlier after documented loss, theft or irreparable damage | Days of interruption in medical need after which a new rental period and cap start | New order needed to restart the rental after an interruption |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Inexpensive or Routinely Purchased Equipment | 60 | Yes | Yes | 60 | Yes |
| Capped Rental Equipment | 60 | Yes | Yes | 60 | Yes |
| Continuous Positive Airway Pressure Equipment | 60 | Yes | Yes | 60 | Yes |
| Power Mobility Device | 60 | Yes | Yes | 60 | Yes |
| Oxygen and Oxygen Equipment | 60 | Yes | Yes | 60 | Yes |
| Frequently Serviced Equipment | 60 | Yes | Yes | 60 | Yes |
| Customized Equipment | 60 | Yes | Yes | 60 | Yes |

## Reading the figures

- The figures are the same in all seven classes: a reasonable useful lifetime of 60 months, replacement payable after that lifetime, earlier replacement payable after documented loss, theft or irreparable damage, an interruption figure of 60 days, and a new order needed to restart the rental after an interruption.
- The lifetime is counted in months; the interruption figure is counted in days.

**What length of interruption in medical need is the reference point for a new rental period in Customized Equipment?** 60 days, as in every other class.

**Is a new order needed to restart a rental after an interruption in Oxygen and Oxygen Equipment?** Yes; every class requires a new order to restart the rental after an interruption.
